newsitem.title: USA: First Union raises performance targets.
newsitem.headline: First Union raises performance targets.

text.p: First Union Corp, as expected, raised several internal performance targets used the in the banking industry to benchmark profitability.
First Union, the sixth-largest U.S. bank holding company, said it was aiming for return on common equity (ROE) of 18-20 percent, compared to the previous target of 16-17 percent.

First Union said it is now targeting return on average assets (ROA) of 1.30-1.50 percent, compared to a previous guideline of 1.00-1.10 percent. It said the new guideline for earnings per share growth is a 10-13 range cmpared to the previous 10 percent target.

First Union said it will begin using five additional performance goals for the first time. One of the new targets is an overhead efficiency ratio of 53-57 percent. The ratio is calculated by dividing expenses by revenue. As the percentage drops, efficiency rises.
First Union said other guidelines include a leverage ratio of 6.00-7.00 percent, net charge-offs of 50-65 basis points and a dividend payout of 30-35 percent.

In addition, the goal for First Union's fee-based businesses such as investment banking and asset management is to generate 40 percent of company revenue by the year 2000, up from the current 30 percent.
First Union said its goal for its Capital Management Group is to grow pre-tax net income from $220 million in 1995 to as much as $1.15 billion in the year 2000.
First Union said the goal for the Capital Markets Group is to grow pre-tax net income from $289 million in 1995 to as much as $760 million in the year 2000.

First Union said its strategy is to leverage its investments in fee-based businesses such as investment banking and asset managements, and maximize the return on its investments in new technology. It said the strategy will help it meet its goals of higher revenues and enhanced productivity.

"We intend to leverage the resources and possibilities of the $134 billion company we have built over the past decade," said First Union Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Edward Crutchfield said in a statement.

"These new performance guidelines will create a strict 'burden of proof' that will guide our strategic decisions regarding capital allocation, ensuring that we maintain a laser-sharp focus on creating additional shareholder value."

He continued, "First Union has already achieved the size, scale and geographic diversity necessary to succeed, and is now poised to set the standard for superior financial performance in our industry."
